item.title: Inaugural CMG World Robot Mount Tai Competition enters qualifying phase
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 16:55:00
Robot at the inaugural CMG World Robot Mount Tai Challenge in Tai'an, East China's Shandong Province Photo: Courtesy of CMG The inaugural CMG World Robot Mount Tai Competition entered the qualifying phase on Monday, with test runs underway ahead of the main event scheduled for November 2 in Tai'an, East China's Shandong Province. The competition has drawn broad attention from across the robotics industry and features four events: a humanoid robot speed race, a legged robot speed race, a legged robot load-carrying race, and an all-terrain scouting challenge. The race course follows the hiking route from Hongmen to Zhongtianmen on Mount Tai, stretching 3.8 kilometers and including more than 3,100 stone steps. Known for its steep stairways and sharp turns, the route is designed to test robots' motion control, environmental perception, dynamic balance and overall adaptability. Organizers said the event aims to turn Mount Tai's natural terrain into a "natural extreme testing ground," helping robots move closer to real-world applications. Renowned for its grueling terrain, Mount Tai is one of China's most iconic peaks. Beyond its cultural and historical significance, it is also known for its long, steep and step-dense climbing routes, which typically take hikers two to three hours to get to the top. Among the participants is "Walker Taishan" or "Xingzhe Taishan" in Chinese, a Yobotics E1 humanoid robot developed by Shandong Yobotics Intelligent Robot Co Ltd. It is the first robot in the industry to attempt climbing Mount Tai. Standing 1.38 meters tall and weighing 39 kilograms, Walker Taishan combines Chinese cultural symbolism with advanced technological design. Its name reflects both the spirit of determined progress and the steadfastness associated with Mount Tai, embodying a fusion of technology and humanity, the company told the Global Times on Monday. The Yobotics E1 features a modular structure that allows it to adapt to stairs, slopes, narrow passages, and rugged or muddy terrain. Equipped with gait-balance algorithms and whole-body coordinated motion control, the robot is designed for high reliability and strong environmental adaptability. Industry experts said that bringing robots into a genuine mountain environment reflects the industry's transition from laboratory demonstrations to validation in complex real-world scenarios. The event has attracted active participation from companies across the robotics supply chain. Thermal management is one telling example: continuous load-bearing climbs place enormous demands on joint motors and whole-machine heat dissipation. Shanghai-based Wenqing Intelligent Control, a Chinese company specializing in robotic thermal management systems and embodied AI infrastructure, has used air-cooling and liquid-cooling technologies to maintain stable temperatures in its components, improving performance and reliability during prolonged, high-intensity operation. As the competition draws near, participating robots are undergoing final-round field testing and optimization at a mountain-climbing training ground at the foot of Mount Tai. Built by Shandong CCRC Technology Group, the facility replicates Mount Tai's 3.8-kilometer climbing route and more than 3,100 steps. It includes 11 test tracks designed to assess robots' perception, balance, motion control, gait transitions, and obstacle-crossing abilities in complex environments. Engineers said that the training is intended to help robots adapt to a wide range of real-world conditions and enhance their ability to recognize road surfaces and resist slipping, ensuring stable performance in the competition. Although the simulated track is highly challenging, the actual route on Mount Tai is even more demanding. Worn stone steps, uneven step heights, gravel-covered surfaces all place greater strain on the robots' vision system and mobility. Wang Debao, senior vice president of Shandong CCRC, told the Global Times on Monday that researchers have built a specialized training site designed to challenge humanoid and quadruped robots with a series of realistic mountain-climbing tasks. The track features a continuous series of climbing steps, along with challenging features such as steps that are difficult for robots to detect, steep and slippery narrow steps, and S-shaped steps. The training site is also equipped with ramps alongside the track, rest platforms, and a safety hanging system. These facilities form a complete testing system that comprehensively evaluates key capabilities including environmental perception, dynamic balance, motion control, gait switching, and fault tolerance during obstacle crossing, Wang noted. In recent years, rapid advances in AI, motion control, sensor fusion and new materials have helped humanoid and legged robots move beyond demonstrations into practical applications such as inspection, rescue, logistics and tourism. Organizers said that hosting the first CMG World Robot Mount Tai Competition will help Tai'an seize future opportunities and strengthen its competitiveness. The city will also use the event to deepen cooperation among industry, universities and research institutes, while attracting high-quality robotics projects. Global Times

item.title: Follow-up investigation identifies surface rupture zone from magnitude-7.0 Baqen earthquake for the first time
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 16:21:00
Photo: Screenshot from CCTV A field team from the China Earthquake Administration and members of the local earthquake agency of Southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region identified the first surface rupture zone on Sunday caused by the magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Baqen County in Nagqu in the region, China Central Television reported on Monday, citing the administration. The rupture zone discovered by the field team is located about 15 kilometers east of the epicenter and 20 kilometers from Maru Township, according to the administration. The investigation found that the earthquake was characterized primarily by normal faulting, accompanied by some left-lateral strike-slip movement. The rupture surface was nearly vertical, with a maximum depth of 3.5 meters and left-lateral displacement about 0.9 meters. The rupture zone was 8 to 30 meters wide and extended into the snow-covered mountains to the north and south, the administration said. The investigation also identified multiple instances of soil liquefaction and ground fissures, indicating that the earthquake had caused geological damage over a relatively wide area, according to the administration. Global Times

item.title: A cyclone to hit Himalayas and bring extreme snowfall to Xizang region? China's meteorological authority debunks rumors
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 14:31:00
Sunrise over the snow-capped peaks of the Himalayas Photo: IC The China Meteorological Administration (CMA) on Monday debunked online claims that a tropical cyclone forming over the Bay of Bengal between October 26 and October 31 would "slam into the Himalayas" and bring exceptionally heavy snowfall to the southwestern part of China's Xizang Autonomous Region, clarifying that the storm could affect southern Xizang but that the description of the online claims was inaccurate. According to Dong Lin, chief forecaster at China's National Meteorological Center (NMC), a tropical depression is currently active over the Bay of Bengal and is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm on Monday, with its strength comparable to the tropical storm category used in China. After forming, the storm is forecast to move westward initially and continue to intensify, potentially reaching the level of a very severe cyclonic storm, with sustained winds of 33 to 38 meters per second. The storm is expected to make landfall along India's eastern coast on October 28 as a severe or very severe cyclonic storm before turning northward and gradually weakening, chinanews.com.cn reported. Given the limitations of the forecast period, forecasts of the storm's post-landfall track and intensity remain uncertain. By the time it approaches the Himalayas, the system is expected to have weakened into a weak residual vortex, making online claims that the cyclone will "slam into" the Himalayas inaccurate, and its main body is impossible to cross the mountain range, Dong said. The NMC forecasts notable rain and snow across central and eastern Xizang on Friday and Saturday as a Bay of Bengal storm moves northward and interacts with a plateau trough. Shannan Prefecture, Xigaze and Lhasa in Xizang could see moderate to heavy snow or sleet, while parts of the southern border may experience heavy to exceptionally heavy snowfall, with 10 to 30 millimeters of precipitation and 5 to 25 centimeters of new snow accumulation. According to Chen Tao, chief forecaster from the NMC, the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau's high terrain acts as a natural barrier, preventing the Bay of Bengal storm from crossing it. The heavy precipitation and snow forecast for southern Xizang is not directly attributable to the cyclone itself crossing the mountains, Chen told the Global Times on Monday. Chen explained that on Friday and Saturday, the circulation of the northward-moving Bay of Bengal storm is expected to drive southerly winds, continuously transporting warm, moist air toward the plateau. When this moisture encounters the southern slopes of the Himalayas, it will be forced upward. The orographic uplift along the southern slopes of the Himalayas will trigger heavy rain and snow. An eastward-moving westerly trough is expected to interact with the Bay of Bengal storm, boosting moisture transport and atmospheric uplift and intensifying precipitation. The storm's circulation is forecast to weaken on November 1, bringing a significant reduction in rain and snow across southern Xizang, Chen said. According to Chen, the storm's evolution will be influenced by the westerly trough, the subtropical high and South Asia's terrain. If it weakens rapidly after landfall, reduced moisture transport could alter the intensity and distribution of precipitation in southern Xizang, requiring continuous monitoring and updated forecasts. According to Dong, whether heavy snowfall occurs in southwestern Xizang will depend not only on the cyclone's track but also on the strength and position of the plateau trough, the residual vortex's intensity and moisture transport efficiency. As the forecast period is relatively long, the actual snowfall intensity and accumulation remain uncertain.

item.title: Lula's reelection brings continuity to China-Brazil ties, fresh momentum for Global South cooperation: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 12:56:00
Brazilian incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, presidential candidate of the ruling Workers' Party, displays a national flag of Brazil after casting his ballot at a polling station in Sao Bernardo do Campo, Brazil, Oct. 25, 2026. (Photo by Paulo Lopes/Xinhua) "Thank you, Brazilian people," Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva wrote on social media on Sunday night after securing a historic fourth presidential term in a dramatic electoral comeback. Lula's victory has drawn international attention not only for its implications for Latin America's shifting political landscape, but also for the future of China-Brazil relations, with prospects for deeper economic cooperation, sustained high-level diplomatic engagement and closer coordination within BRICS and other multilateral frameworks coming into focus. With 99.96 percent of the votes counted, Lula received 51.78 percent of the valid votes, compared with 48.22 percent for Flavio Bolsonaro, the Liberal Party's presidential candidate and son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, according to the official tally, the Xinhua News Agency reported. Lula will be sworn in on January 5, 2027, for a four-year term, marking his fourth election as Brazil's president. The victory marked the first time a presidential candidate in Brazil had overturned a first-round deficit to win a runoff election. According to Xinhua, Brazil's presidential election follows a two-round majoritarian system. To win in the first round, held on October 4, a candidate must secure more than half of the valid votes. Flavio Bolsonaro finished ahead of incumbent Lula, winning about 47 percent of the valid votes against Lula's roughly 45 percent. As neither candidate crossed the 50-percent threshold, the two advanced to a runoff, which Lula won. The election outcome comes amid significant political shifts across Latin America and growing geopolitical competition in the region. International media have highlighted the implications of Lula's victory for Brazil's relations with major powers, particularly China and the US, as well as the country's role in promoting cooperation among Global South nations. The South China Morning Post reported on Monday that Lula's reelection would extend the tenure of an administration under which Chinese investment in Brazil had reached record levels. Pan Deng, director of the Latin America and Caribbean Region Law Center at the China University of Political Science and Law, told the Global Times on Monday that Lula's reelection has provided stability and predictability for China-Brazil relations over the next four years. Pan said the political consensus reached by the two countries' leaders during Lula's 2023 visit to China, together with sustained high-level exchanges, has strengthened mutual trust and provided strategic guidance for bilateral ties. Despite potential constraints from a conservative Congress, cooperation with China enjoys broad support across Brazil's political spectrum and is unlikely to be significantly affected by domestic political divisions, he added. China's top diplomat Wang Yi met with Special Advisor to the President of Brazil Celso Amorim on September 16 in Beijing. Amorim said Brazil stands ready to work with China to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state and inject new connotations into building a Brazil-China community with a shared future for a more just world and a more sustainable planet, Xinhua reported. China has remained Brazil's largest trading partner for years, with bilateral economic ties forming a major pillar of the broader relationship. Trade between Brazil and China reached a record $143.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, reinforcing China's position as Brazil's largest trading partner. Brazilian exports to the Chinese market totaled $84.7 billion between January and September, an increase of 12 percent compared with the same period in 2025. Imports from China rose 9.9 percent to $58.6 billion. The figures were released by Brazil's Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services (MDIC) and compiled by the Brazil-China Business Council (CEBC), according to a report published by Valor Econômico and covered by Brasil 247. Looking ahead, Pan identified three areas with significant growth potential for China-Brazil cooperation: green and low-carbon development, including renewable energy and environmental protection; the digital economy and artificial intelligence, particularly in agriculture and AI governance; and expanded aerospace cooperation, building on the two countries' longstanding satellite partnership to advance remote-sensing applications in agriculture, disaster prevention and logistics. Xu Shicheng, vice president of the China Society of Latin American Studies, told the Global Times on Monday that Lula's reelection could also help take China-Brazil relations to a new level, as bilateral cooperation has expanded beyond traditional commodity trade into emerging sectors such as electric vehicles, renewable energy, infrastructure and advanced technologies. Beyond specific industries, Chinese analysts also pointed out that the Lula administration's emphasis on strategic autonomy and economic development aimed at improving people's livelihoods aligns closely with China's pursuit of high-quality development and open, inclusive international cooperation. At the multilateral level, Lula's reelection is also expected to provide continuity for Brazil's participation in BRICS and broader Global South cooperation, they noted. China and Brazil could continue coordinating their positions on reform of the United Nations and World Trade Organization, global debt restructuring and international climate negotiations, helping ensure that global governance arrangements better reflect the concerns and development needs of emerging economies, Pan said. The two countries could also jointly initiate inclusive cooperation projects targeting developing nations, providing additional opportunities for Global South countries to participate in international economic and technological cooperation. Pan said such initiatives could contribute to a more equitable international development environment and strengthen the collective voice of developing countries in global affairs. The election has also attracted attention for its potential implications for Latin America's political landscape. Reuters reported that Lula's victory came against the backdrop of recent electoral gains by right-wing political forces in several Latin American countries, raising questions about how Brazil's regional diplomacy might evolve during his next term. Pan argued that Lula's victory should not simply be viewed as a return of a particular ideological camp, but rather as a pragmatic response by Brazilian voters to economic and social challenges, including high inflation and poverty pressures associated with neoliberal policies. The outcome could strengthen Latin America's pursuit of independent development and inject fresh momentum into regional integration, he said. Xu noted that Lula could face considerable domestic political challenges during his fourth term, as right-wing and center-right forces secured significant representation in Brazil's Congress. Nevertheless, he said Lula's previous poverty alleviation and social welfare policies have retained support among lower-income voters, while his administration is expected to continue prioritizing BRICS cooperation and Brazil's role in the Global South. The election also sends a message that Latin American countries can pursue development paths suited to their own national conditions rather than relying on Western-led models, while expanding diversified international partnerships, Pan said. He added that the result reflects growing regional aspirations for independent decision-making and resistance to external interference.

item.title: 20th CPC Central Committee starts fifth plenary session
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 12:03:00
CHINA / POLITICS 20th CPC Central Committee starts fifth plenary session By Xinhua Published: Oct 26, 2026 12:03 PM
The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) started its fifth plenary session in Beijing on Monday morning. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a work report on behalf of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and expounded on a draft decision of the CPC Central Committee on some major issues concerning strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance. The draft decision summarizes the achievements and experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era in a truth-seeking manner, and offers in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks concerning Party building at present and for some time to come. It also sets out strategic plans for strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, according to a Political Bureau meeting in September that decided to submit the document to the plenum for review. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the full and rigorous Party self-governance has made significant progress, opened up a new frontier for the century-old Party in self-reform, and brought about historic achievements and transformations in the cause of the Party and the country, said an earlier Political Bureau meeting in July that set the plenum's agenda. The meeting said the Party and the people have won the historical initiative to build a strong Party and country, but noted that as profound changes unfold in the world, in China and within the Party, efforts to exercise full and rigorous Party self-governance also face many new circumstances and challenges. It called for adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to uphold and apply the valuable experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era, resolve the prominent issues facing Party building, and consolidate and develop the sound political environment created through Party self-supervision and self-governance.

item.title: China's state security authority warns of data security risks from discarded industrial equipment
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 09:45:00
Photo: China's Ministry of State Security China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) warned on its WeChat account on Monday that improperly disposed-of industrial equipment and specialized instruments could pose risks to commercial secrets, critical infrastructure and national security, as sensitive data may remain recoverable even after files are deleted or storage devices are formatted. According to the article the MSS posted, some organizations mistakenly believe that deleting files or formatting hard drives is sufficient before selling or disposing of outdated equipment. However, such operations generally remove only file indexes, leaving underlying data potentially recoverable through specialized techniques. Conventional file deletion or formatting does not necessarily erase the underlying information, the article noted. Even equipment that appears to have reached the end of its service life may still contain sensitive corporate or industry data. The risks vary across sectors, potentially affecting corporate interests, the security of critical industries and national security, according to the article. In critical infrastructure sectors such as energy, telecommunications, transportation, chemicals and water management, retired industrial control systems and programmable controllers may contain operational parameters, facility layouts and security configurations. If acquired by overseas organizations, such information could be used to identify system vulnerabilities and security weaknesses, potentially facilitating cyberattacks or physical sabotage, the MSS warned. The article also highlighted risks associated with secondhand surveying and monitoring equipment, including GPS receivers and geological exploration instruments. Such devices may retain high-precision coordinates, terrain data and mineral exploration records, potentially including sensitive geographical information related to military-controlled areas, classified facilities and strategic infrastructure projects, the MSS said. Foreign intelligence agencies could also seek to acquire discarded industrial equipment and storage media from sensitive sectors through secondhand trading platforms or recycling channels, the article warned. Such equipment could be used to recover sensitive information or reverse-engineer system architectures, control logic and security vulnerabilities. Some buyers may offer unusually high prices while specifically targeting industrial enterprises and research institutions. To mitigate these risks, the article called for stricter management of discarded equipment, emphasizing that secure data destruction should take place before devices are sold or transferred. For equipment containing critical data, physical degaussing or destruction of storage media should be prioritized to prevent information recovery, according to the article. The article also recommended using qualified recycling and disposal providers rather than casually selling industrial equipment through secondhand platforms, while ensuring that the disposal process is properly documented. It further urged organizations to exercise caution when approached by buyers offering unusually high prices for discarded equipment, and to verify their identities and qualifications. Global Times

item.title: Washington's 'shutdown' is choking off its own future: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 22:38:00
China US Illustration: Chen Xia/GT As capital from many countries flows into China at an accelerating pace, US investors - constrained by their own country's rules - can only watch as their window of opportunity narrows. Washington should listen carefully to the concerns of US farmers, pharmaceutical companies and investors, and weigh the costs of imposing restrictions. The US Treasury recently released a revised proposed rule on outbound investment restrictions inviting public comments through December 7. In addition to the existing restricted sectors of semiconductor technologies and microelectronics, artificial intelligence systems and quantum information technologies, the proposal seeks to bring supercomputing and hypersonic systems under more detailed controls, while adding biotechnology to the list and designating China and other countries as "countries of concern." On October 24, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) responded to "a recent US Treasury proposal that would expand and intensify restrictions on outbound investment in China," calling it a discriminatory move and a typical practice of overstretching the concept of national security. The proposed rules "run counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state," the MOFCOM spokesperson said. China will closely follow further developments and reserve the right to retaliate, the spokesperson noted. The steady tightening of US investment controls is an attempt to contain China's emerging industries by stretching the concept of national security beyond its proper bounds. From the 2023 executive order to the expansion of the scope of restrictions through congressional legislation in 2025, and now the addition of biotechnology, the underlying logic remains consistent: to slow China's technological progress by cutting off capital flows. The irony is that biotechnology, the latest sector to be brought under the restrictions, is also one of the most active areas of mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries. One-third of the world's innovative drugs in development come from China. This year, US pharmaceutical companies such as Pfizer and Bristol Myers Squibb have reached licensing agreements worth billions of dollars with their Chinese partners. Meanwhile, the US pharmaceutical industry has spent months lobbying against Washington's proposed stringent investment restrictions. Under the guise of national security, what amounts to protectionism is first and foremost tying the hands of US investors themselves. Data show that Washington's policy direction is running directly counter to the market choices of most US companies. According to MOFCOM, investment from major sources including the US, South Korea, France and Switzerland continued to grow from January to September, with investment from the US increasing by 7.7 percent. Despite the political noise, most US companies are still putting their money where their confidence in the Chinese market lies. On the other hand, the 7.7 percent growth rate was significantly lower than France's 31.8 percent and Switzerland's 26 percent, showing that Washington's restrictive measures are having a negative impact on corporate decision-making. Member Survey 2026 by the US-China Business Council found that 95 percent of respondents considered their China operations to be "somewhat to very important for staying competitive globally." The direction in which the market is voting of its own accord is precisely the opposite of the direction in which policymakers are trying to pull it. Facts confirm that countries shutting their doors often end up sacrificing their own opportunities. According to the US-China Business Council survey, US exports to China fell 26 percent last year, resulting in the loss of approximately 148,000 jobs. Among US companies affected by their own country's export controls, 61 percent have watched their market share shift to competitors. International Data Corporation predicts that Washington's trade restrictions could leave the US' humanoid robotics market nearly 60 percent smaller than it would otherwise be by 2030. "Once markets are lost, they are hard to regain," US business leaders have warned. By contrast, foreign investment in China's high-tech sector increased 33.8 percent year on year from January to September, while reinvestment of profits by foreign-invested enterprises rose 4.7 percent. The magnetic pull of China's vast market remains strong and continues to grow. As capital from many countries around the world flows into China at an accelerating pace, US investors constrained by their own country's rules can only watch as their window of opportunity narrows. China-US economic and trade relationship is built on mutual benefit and win-win outcomes, and it must not be undermined by the countercurrent of politicization and securitization. The strategic guidance provided by the heads of state of China and the US, along with the cooperative ties painstakingly built by businesses on both sides, should not be eroded by a proposed rule. China-US cooperation is vital to the well-being of the peoples of both countries, to the stability of global industrial and supply chains and to the growth of the world economy. Labeling legitimate business activities as "threats" and weaponizing capital flows undermine not only business confidence but also the foundations of the international economic and trade order. The proposed rule is still at the consultation stage, and its final text has yet to be determined. The rational voices of the US business community deserve to be heard. While reserving the right to take countermeasures at any time, China will continue to counter external uncertainties through high-standard opening-up. The proposition that "investing in China means investing in the future" will only become more evident. Washington should listen carefully to the concerns of US farmers, pharmaceutical companies and investors, and weigh the costs of imposing restrictions. The ropes used to trip others up often end up binding one's own hands first. The simple truth that cooperation benefits both sides while confrontation harms both is one Washington would do well to heed.

item.title: GT Voice: Shipbuilding industry is defined by both competition and cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 21:59:00
The world's first 41,800-ton bidirectional sailing self-discharging ship delivers in East China's Jiangsu Province on July 21. Photo: Guo Yuandanz/GT New data from China's shipbuilding industry has drawn widespread media attention. China continues to lead the world in three key indicators, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) reported. In the first nine months of this year, Chinese shipyards completed 58.05 million deadweight tons (DWT) of shipbuilding output, a year on year rise of 50.7 percent. New ship orders hit 175.29 million DWT, surging 163.2 percent year on year. As of the end of September, the order backlog stood at 399.13 million DWT, up 64.8 percent from a year earlier. Notably, China's new ship orders accounted for 81.8 percent of the global market, MIIT statistics showed. These figures amount to more than a demonstration of the country's manufacturing scale. Shipbuilding is a capital-intensive, long-cycle and technology-heavy industry. When ship owners place orders, they are not simply comparing quotations. They are making decisions on fleet capacity, asset values and delivery security. Choosing a shipyard is, in effect, a vote of confidence in an entire industrial system: its suppliers, engineers, project managers, skilled workers and ability to deliver as promised. China's expanding order book reflects not only the available capacity, but also the market's assessment of its supply-chain coordination and execution. What deserves more attention than the sheer volume of orders is their structural composition. New orders are not evenly distributed across all vessel types, but are heavily concentrated in the segments with the strictest green compliance requirements and the highest technological complexity. In the first three quarters, China's global market share in new orders for green-powered ships reached 74.1 percent, 5.7 percentage points higher than in the first half of the year. This clearly signals that China's leading position in shipbuilding is evolving from the traditional strengths of scale and cost-effectiveness to new competitive edges in green technology, sophisticated vessel construction and industrial synergy. As global maritime environmental regulations tighten and alternative fuel technologies advance, fleet owners are increasingly turning to next-generation vessels powered by methanol, liquefied natural gas and ammonia. Chinese shipyards' remarkable share in green ship orders shows that their capabilities in green design, supply chain coordination and high-standard construction have won widespread market recognition. This advantage is set to prove far more sustainable than a simple cost-and-scale edge. Many foreign media outlets tend to frame the rise of China's shipbuilding sector as a zero-sum game between China and South Korea. But this narrow narrative overlooks the profound changes unfolding across the global shipbuilding industrial chain. The expansion of China's shipbuilding ecosystem has opened up new market space for South Korean component and marine equipment companies. South Korean shipbuilders can leverage China's massive delivery volume and huge supporting demand to expand exports of their high-value-added supporting products. Small and medium-sized South Korean marine equipment makers are accelerating their entry into the Chinese market, with major supporting equipment shipped from South Korea to China including hull safety monitoring systems, marine energy-saving devices and marine engine components. This deep integration not only elevates the supporting quality of Chinese-built vessels, but also gives South Korean companies direct access to the world's largest shipbuilding market. This dynamic of "competition in finished vessels, cooperation in supporting sectors" is far closer to the industrial reality than simplistic zero-sum assumptions. The South Korean shipbuilding industry is facing pressure from labor shortages and challenges from investment in US shipbuilding. Against this backdrop, the value of cooperation becomes ever clearer. Shipbuilding is a long-haul race that rewards sustained technological investment, supply chain resilience and reliable deliveries. Global decarbonization in shipping continues to open up fresh demand. China needs to consolidate its early-mover advantage in green vessels, while South Korea needs a stable export market for the components and a reliable industrial partner. The rise of China's shipbuilding industry brings more diverse, greener supply options to back up the global transition of maritime transport. For competitors such as South Korea, the competition creates some pressure on finished vessels, but it also creates opportunities for component exports, production collaboration and strategic repositioning. So, competition and cooperation has once again proved to be the perpetual norm of doing business.

item.title: Jetta's 'comeback' in China proves the move was right
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 20:04:00
Screenshot of the Jetta M6 Photo: Jetta official website Once synonymous with rugged reliability and the brand that gave millions of Chinese families their "first car," Jetta has recently returned to the spotlight. On October 22, FAW-Volkswagen's Jetta brand unveiled its battery electric vehicle, the M6, in China. Priced at under 100,000 yuan (about $15,000) even in its top trim, the model comes equipped with advanced urban navigation on autopilot driver-assistance features. It surpassed 10,000 locked orders within just 19 hours of launch. This figure may not be staggering in China's fiercely competitive new-energy vehicle sector, yet the market response merits close attention - especially for a legacy automaker racing to embrace electrification. More than just sales performance for a single new model, it points to broader potential for China-Germany automotive industrial cooperation. Earlier, FAW and the Volkswagen Group signed a strategic cooperation agreement in Wolfsburg, Germany. Under the deal, the two sides will jointly roll out 11 China-customized models starting in 2026, spanning battery electric, plug-in hybrid and range-extender electric powertrains. Jetta's electric transformation forms an integral part of this roadmap. More than 30 years ago, the Jetta served as a bridge between German engineering quality and China's mass market. Unlike the old "German technology, assembled in China" model, the new agreement elevates the Chinese side beyond manufacturing and market execution to deep involvement in product definition and research and development (R&D), with the Chinese partner taking the lead in selected areas. German manufacturing expertise and engineering standards, paired with China's mature battery, smart-cabin and autonomous-driving solutions as well as local supply chains, create distinctive synergy. This revives the iconic national car with German roots for a new era. The Jetta M6's market reception serves as a real-world test of this collaborative framework. Beneath China-Germany automotive cooperation lies four decades of integration and mutual trust. Since the establishment of SAIC Volkswagen Automotive Co Ltd in the 1980s, which marked the beginning of joint ventures in China's passenger car industry, the partnership has continued to evolve, with successive contract renewals in recent years and increased investment in local R&D. The rationale behind the cooperation has long since moved beyond its original model. Volkswagen has built in Hefei, East China's Anhui Province its first R&D center outside Germany, with the capacity to fully develop and validate products, cutting the overall vehicle development cycle by 30 percent. A growing body of practice shows that aligned technologies, talent pools, supply chains and market demands from both countries can generate a competitive edge greater than the sum of its parts. Against various external speculations, China has demonstrated its commitment to high-standard opening-up through verifiable institutional arrangements. It rejects closed, exclusive blocs. Foreign automakers receive full national treatment on permits, standards and subsidies. Foreign brands account for one-third of sales under China renews auto trade-in subsidy program. China's Ministry of Commerce has held repeated exchanges with the German Association of the Automotive Industry, welcoming and encouraging German enterprises to deepen their footprint in China and expand local R&D and investment. It also advocates managing frictions and differences through dialogue and consultation to keep the global automotive supply chain stable and unimpeded. Jetta's electric "comeback" in China is a tangible industrial manifestation of this openness. "Volkswagen Jetta, a rational choice" remains Jetta's most classic and widely recognized tagline.
